title: Chapter 63
content:
Pacing across the lawn, Jakyeong stopped by the edge of the pool, staring down into the water. Underwater spotlights illuminated the basin, casting rippling turquoise patterns across the night.

After dinner, Park Tae-soo had delivered their first operational target dossier: a man named Choi Man-sik, the late Choi Ki-tae’s uncle.

Following his brother’s demise, Man-sik had seized control of the syndicate's distribution networks. Discovering that Il-hyun was behind Ki-tae's decapitation, he had aligned himself with Chairman Kang's camp, constantly stirring up friction. To make matters worse, the bastard had begun peddling narcotics to underage trainees at Haewon’s entertainment subsidiary.

The three operatives had spent over an hour reviewing the logistics before Jakyeong, feeling suffocated, slipped out for fresh air. An afternoon shower had left the manicured turf damp, the humid air sticking heavily to his lungs with every breath.

As he turned to head inside, his phone buzzed with an incoming video call from Sasha.

Checking the grounds to ensure no guards were lingering nearby, he hit accept. Sasha’s face illuminated the screen, breaking into a radiant, relieved smile.

[Wei! What on earth happened? You vanished into thin air without a single word!]

Jakyeong offered an awkward, apologetic grin. "Things came up. I won't be returning anytime soon."

Her expression instantly fell.

[Han left too... Rita is beside herself with grief.] She hesitated, biting her lip before continuing softly: [And so am I. I really thought... you felt something special for me.]

He didn't catch every nuance of her Russian, but her sorrow was unmistakable.

Just as guilt pinched his chest, a face loomed abruptly over his shoulder.

Gasp!

Before Jakyeong could spin around, large fingers snatched the phone straight from his grip like a daikon pulled from soft earth.

Kang Il-hyun stared down into the screen, flashing a dazzling smile as he spoke in flawless, native Russian:

[He's my lover. Never contact him again.]

Before Jakyeong could even process the man's linguistic fluency, Il-hyun casually tossed the phone into the pool.

Jakyeong lunged, but too late—the device hit the water with a splash, sinking to the illuminated bottom. He dove in, scooping the dripping phone from the deep end, only to find the screen fried into static.

Yet the fried electronics were the least of his concerns.

Jakyeong burst from the surface, glaring murderously at the man crouching on the coping with an amused grin. Reaching out, Il-hyun caught Jakyeong’s chin, turning his dripping face from side to side to inspect him. When Jakyeong swatted the hand away with a ferocious slap, Il-hyun ground his teeth with a low, menacing hiss.

"Usually, when subordinates fail to listen, I take their ears. But with my darling... I wonder which piece I should sever to make you obey?"

"Get the fuck away from me."

"Then again, you're so exceptionally handsome that you'd probably look striking even without ears."

When fingers reached for his earlobe, Jakyeong snapped, "You're a raving psychopath!"

Il-hyun put on an expression of delicate, wounded grief—a display so transparently fake it was sickening. "Is it that obvious?"

"..."

"They say we're just people with wounded hearts. So be gentle with me, darling. Shower me with love and affection. Hmm?"

Talking to a brick wall.

Shuddering in pure revulsion, Jakyeong hoisted himself out of the pool. Water cascaded from his clothes onto the deck. Il-hyun stepped up behind him, unfurling a plush bath towel to dry him off.

Jakyeong shoved the man's shoulder aside and stormed away, only for Il-hyun to hook an arm around his waist, hoist him onto his broad shoulder, and hurl him straight back into the pool.

SPLASH!

It happened so fast Jakyeong had zero time to react. Breaching the surface, he wiped the water from his eyes, glaring in sheer disbelief.

"Cool off your temper before you come out," Il-hyun chuckled from the edge. "I'll wait."

Jakyeong dragged himself onto the stone deck, lunging at the smug bastard with every intention of tearing his throat out.

Wang Han dropped ice into his tumbler, poured a measure of high-proof whiskey, and took a slow sip.

He glanced back at the surveillance photo Park Tae-soo had provided. Choi Man-sik—a ruthless cartel boss involved in narcotics trafficking and illicit organ harvesting. Shaved bald with tribal ink crawling up his throat, the man possessed the face of a hardened butcher.

They needed to coordinate the hit around the target’s transit schedule, but Jakyeong, who had stepped out for air, hadn't returned.

From the window, Wang Ryun burst into a loud laugh. Han walked over to look.

Down in the illuminated pool, Jakyeong and Kang Il-hyun were violently grappling in the water, sending waves splashing over the coping.

"What in the world are those two doing?"

"Beats me," Ryun snickered. "Looks like a lover's quarrel. Wei just landed a solid right hook on President Kang’s cheekbone."

"Jesus Christ... How long have they been at it?"

"About five minutes. Should we go break it up?"

Han shook his head. Even from a distance, it was clear that rather than an outright brawl, Il-hyun was effortlessly humoring the kid's tantrums.

Soaked to the bone, Jakyeong finally climbed out and collapsed onto a sun lounger. Moments later, Il-hyun emerged, wrapping a towel around Jakyeong’s head and gently rubbing his hair dry.

After trading blows in the water, the scene now looked shockingly domestic.

"He's surprisingly attentive," Ryun mused. "Does he actually have real feelings for Wei?"

"Don't be naive," Han warned. "He's using us. A man like that doesn't know the meaning of trust."

As Han turned back toward the table, Ryun let out a low whistle. "Whoa... look at that."

Han stepped back to the glass.

Il-hyun had leaned over the lounger, capturing Jakyeong’s mouth in an uninvited kiss from behind while Jakyeong thrashed against the hold.

Ryun whipped out his phone to snap a photo, prompting Han to smack the back of his head. "Stop messing with the kid."

"I'm just having fun! Who would've thought our little assassin would end up tangled with a man?"

Han dragged Ryun back to the sectional by his collar. As they were packing the intelligence files into a courier pouch, a sharp knock rattled the door.

Jakyeong burst inside, dripping wet and fuming.

"Using your shower."

Without waiting for a reply, he stormed into the bathroom and slammed the door. Ryun poked his head into the hallway to check if Il-hyun had followed, but the corridor was empty. Through the bathroom door, Jakyeong’s muffled curses echoed loudly over the rush of the water.

After soaking in a steaming tub to soothe his bruised muscles, Jakyeong threw on a set of Ryun’s oversized loungewear and stepped into the living room.

There sat Kang Il-hyun, comfortably sharing drinks with the Wang brothers. Freshly showered and dressed in crisp linen, he looked effortlessly polished. Smoke hung thick in the air, the coffee table crowded with top-shelf liquor, crystal glasses, and platters of fresh fruit.

Wang Han remained stone-faced and sober, while Ryun was already visibly tipsy.

"Over here, Wei! Come have a drink!"

Jakyeong wanted to ignore the invitation, but Il-hyun caught his eye, offering a subtle, beckoning tilt of his chin. Fearing Ryun’s loose lips might spill sensitive operational secrets, Jakyeong reluctantly took a seat on the leather sectional.

Instead of hard liquor, Il-hyun popped a chilled bottle of vintage champagne, pouring a flute for Jakyeong.

Golden bubbles danced to the surface. As Jakyeong lifted the crystal, Il-hyun casually draped an arm along the sofa back, his forearm resting against Jakyeong’s shoulder. Jakyeong debated shoving it off, but decided against a scene, picking up a slice of cold watermelon instead.

Seeing the tactical dossiers scattered across the table, he assumed they’d been discussing the hit on Choi Man-sik.

"And then what happened?" Il-hyun asked smoothly, turning to Ryun.

Ryun leaned in, thoroughly entertained. "After that, he dated all across the map! Italian girls, Vietnamese girls, Spanish girls... Ah! What was that Spanish girl's name again? Veronica?"

Pfft!

Jakyeong choked on his champagne, spitting a fine mist across the table.

They weren't discussing the hit at all—they were dissecting his dating history.

Jakyeong glared daggers at Ryun, but his older brother was on a roll.

"Anyway, she was drop-dead gorgeous—and had a body that wouldn't quit. Right, Wei?"

Jakyeong shot him a frantic slit-throat gesture, but Ryun merely grinned, tossing in the final nail:

"You were crazy about her, weren't you?"

"Is that so?" Il-hyun purred, his voice dropping into a low, velvety register. "Our darling was crazy about her, was he?"

Sensing the sudden shift in temperature, Wang Han shoved a large slice of watermelon straight into Ryun’s open mouth. "Shut up and eat."

Ryun swatted Han's hand away, spitting seeds. "I hate watermelon! Wei’s the one who loves watermelon!"

"Starting tonight, you love it too," Han hissed through his teeth. "Shut the fuck up and chew."

Il-hyun watched the exchange with a serene, pleasant smile.

"Please, don't mind me. I'm remarkably open-minded about these matters. The past is in the past, after all."

He turned to Jakyeong, flashing a radiant, dimpled smile that sent an icy shiver straight down Jakyeong's spine.

Shaking the arm from his shoulder, Jakyeong bolted to his feet. Ryun began singing Il-hyun’s praises, marveling at how generous and understanding the corporate boss was, but Jakyeong tuned out the noise entirely.

He shot Han an urgent look to drag Ryun away before offering a stiff nod to the room. "I'm going to sleep. I'm exhausted."

He practically fled the suite, retreating across the hall to his own quarters. He threw the deadbolts on the outer door, secured the bedroom latch, and paced the room.

Ten minutes passed. Then twenty. The corridor remained dead quiet.

I worried over nothing.

Sighing in relief, he stripped off his clothes and prepared to slide beneath the duvet.

Knock, knock.

Jakyeong held his breath, staying dead silent.

The brass handle jiggled violently: Rattle, rattle.

He stood frozen, glaring at the wood. It was unmistakably Kang Il-hyun.

[Stop playing dead and open the door.]

When Jakyeong refused to move a muscle, a low chuckle drifted through the keyhole.

[I'm breaking it down, darling.]

As if he'd actually break down his own door.

Jakyeong kept his ground—

BAM!

The heavy wood ruptured with a concussive crack, the door flying wide open.

Jakyeong’s jaw dropped.

Standing in the doorway with a lit cigarette between his lips was Kang Il-hyun—casually twirling a razor-sharp steel hatchet in his palm.

Where the fuck did he get a hand axe?!

Il-hyun offered an easy, charming grin, spinning the polished blade between his long fingers. "I had these mounted in every hallway as a safety precaution against fires... but I never imagined it would prove this handy."

Bathed in the dim hallway light with a heavy axe in hand, he looked like a bloodthirsty slasher straight out of a horror film.

As Jakyeong scrambled backward onto the mattress, Il-hyun exhaled a long ribbon of gray smoke, closing the distance with slow, deliberate steps.

"I gave it some careful thought... about which piece to sever to make you listen to me."

"What...?" Jakyeong stammered, staring in sheer disbelief.

Il-hyun raised the hatchet high overhead, whipping his arm forward in a blinding arc.

The steel blade flew through the air.

SHING!

The heavy hatchet buried itself inches deep into the headboard—wedged with millimeter precision right between Jakyeong’s parted thighs.

Jakyeong went stark white, staring down at the vibrating steel inches from his groin.

"You psychotic piece of shit...!"

Il-hyun leaned down over the bed, smoke curling from his lips as a depraved, demonic grin spread across his handsome face.

"It's not as if you'll have any use for it going forward anyway... Shall we take it off right now? Hmm?"
